title: Reading Contracts Carefully
text:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. For it to be enforceable, certain elements must be present, namely an offer, an acceptance, and a clear exchange of value, which is known as consideration. Many people sign contracts without reading the terms carefully, which can lead to unexpected obligations. Courts generally expect the parties to honour the written terms, unless one side was misled or forced into signing.

Legal drafters often include a clause that limits liability, stating how much one party can be asked to pay if something goes wrong. Another common provision is the termination clause, which explains how either party may end the agreement early. Some contracts also contain an arbitration clause, requiring disputes to be settled privately rather than in court. Because these clauses can significantly affect your rights, it is wise to seek legal advice before signing.

questions.text: According to the passage, what must be present for a contract to be enforceable?
options: An offer, an acceptance, and a clear exchange of value
A notary's signature and a court date
A written copy kept by a lawyer
A fixed period of at least one year

questions.text: What does the termination clause explain?
options: How much one party can be asked to pay
How either party may end the agreement early
Who is allowed to sign the contract

questions.text: Why might people who sign contracts without reading the terms carefully face problems?
options: Because contracts are always written in a foreign language
Because they may accept obligations they did not expect
Because courts refuse to enforce any written terms
Because arbitration is always more expensive than court

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the final sentence of the second paragraph?
options: To suggest that contracts should be avoided altogether
To encourage readers to get legal advice before signing
To explain how arbitration works step by step
To argue that liability clauses are unfair

vocabulary.definition: having legal force, so that it must be obeyed
able to be made to happen by law
things a person is legally required to do
the act of ending something, such as a contract
settling a dispute with a neutral third party instead of in court

paragraph_translations: Sözleşme, iki veya daha fazla taraf arasında yasal olarak bağlayıcı bir anlaşmadır. Bir sözleşmenin uygulanabilir olması için belirli unsurların bulunması gerekir; bunlar bir teklif, bir kabul ve bedel olarak bilinen açık bir değer alışverişidir. Birçok insan sözleşmeleri şartları dikkatlice okumadan imzalar, bu da beklenmedik yükümlülüklere yol açabilir. Mahkemeler genellikle, taraflardan biri yanıltılmış ya da zorlanarak imzalatılmış olmadıkça, tarafların yazılı şartlara uymasını bekler.

Hukuk metni hazırlayanlar genellikle, bir şey ters giderse bir tarafın ne kadar ödemeye zorlanabileceğini belirten, sorumluluğu sınırlayan bir madde ekler. Bir diğer yaygın hüküm, taraflardan herhangi birinin sözleşmeyi erken nasıl sonlandırabileceğini açıklayan fesih maddesidir. Bazı sözleşmeler ayrıca uyuşmazlıkların mahkemede değil özel olarak çözülmesini gerektiren bir tahkim maddesi içerir. Bu maddeler haklarınızı önemli ölçüde etkileyebileceğinden, imzalamadan önce hukuki danışmanlık almanız akıllıca olur.
